claim: Instruction tuning raises ECE by 13.1% on average and the chat template adds another 2.74% (total +15.8% vs base) on MMLU logit-based confidence across six base/instruct pairs.
stance_target: L2: base versus instruct calibration contrast is established on non-code tasks
quoted_support: On average, instruction tuning boosts accuracy by 3.7% but degrades calibration, increasing ECE by 13.1% and Brier score by 6.5%.

breadth.confidence_families: answer-token logits, P(True), verbalized %, linguistic (Sec 3-5, Table 4)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: yes: base vs instruct vs instruct+chat template (Table 1)
breadth.post_training_stages: instruction tuning vs chat template decoupled; SFT vs RLHF not separated (searched: Sec 3)
breadth.calibration_metrics: ECE (10 bins), Brier score; Wilcoxon and paired bootstrap tests (Sec 3.1, Table 4)
breadth.causal_intervention: answer-framing manipulation (assistant vs user turn), not hidden-state intervention (Sec 5.2)

claim: Models assign up to 26% higher confidence to their own responses than to identical user-provided answers; framing the answer as user input improves calibration by up to 26% without retraining.
scope_conditions: Three elicitation methods (P(True), verbalized, linguistic) on MMLU, GSM8K, TruthfulQA, open-ended MMLU
quoted_support: models assign up to 26% higher confidence to their own responses.
